# How fast is fast enough? Onset-to-isolation delay in the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak (DRC)

Team TAUS (MPPR 2026 group project). A SEIQR transmission model fitted to national surveillance data to 12 Sep 2026, used to compare mean
onset-to-isolation delays of 7, 5 and 3 days at isolation effectiveness of 50%, 80% and 100%.
**Everything is in R; every number, table and figure in the manuscript is generated by the code here.**

## Reproduce
**Option 1: one script.** `Rscript taus_all_in_one.R` runs the unit tests, the whole analysis, and writes all figures, tables and the numbers quoted in the reports (about 9-15 min; needs only `data/` and R + deSolve).
Add `--pdf` to also build the three report PDFs. It is generated from the modular files by `Rscript R/make_single_script.R` (re-run after editing `R/*.R`).

**Option 2: Quarto.** After the R analysis has run (Option 1 or Option 3), render the documents with
```
quarto render quarto/short_report.qmd     # 3-page report (body) + references page
quarto render quarto/fit_report.qmd       # model-fitting report
quarto render quarto/manuscript.qmd       # full manuscript
```
Same text and numbers as the LaTeX versions: prose is Quarto markdown; numbers, tables and the model diagram are LaTeX macros/blocks written by R
(`manuscript/numbers.tex`, `results/tables/*.tex`). The `.qmd` files use the `pdflatex` engine and contain no executable R chunks, so knitr is not needed.

**Option 3: modular scripts.**
```
Rscript R/run_all.R            # tests -> 01..07 -> three PDFs in reports/out/  (~12-15 min, one core)
Rscript R/run_all.R --no-pdf   # analysis only
```
Rebuild only the PDFs (after the analysis has run): `Rscript R/08_build_reports.R`. Outputs in `reports/out/`:
`1_short_report_3pages.pdf` (course report, body <= 3 pages, checked by the script), `2_model_fitting_report.pdf` (fitting process, outcome and code), `3_full_manuscript.pdf`.
No knitr/Quarto is needed; the reports are LaTeX files that read the numbers/tables written by R.

Requirements: R >= 4.3 with package `deSolve` (nothing else; base graphics), and for the PDF a LaTeX distribution with `pdflatex`, `bibtex`
and the packages listed at the top of `manuscript/main.tex` (amsmath, booktabs, natbib, tikz, listings, lineno, hyperref, ...).
Random seeds are fixed in each script; the versions used are written to `results/sessionInfo.txt`.

## Layout
| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `data/bvd_2026/` | Cleaned national surveillance streams (public sources; its own README gives provenance and caveats) |
| `data/cumulative_confirmed_drc.csv` | Official cumulative counts after 12 Sep (UKHSA 27 Sep, CDC 28 Oct), used **only** for validation |
| `R/00_functions.R` | Model, calibration, stochastic engine, constants (`CFG`), helpers |
| `R/01_data_prep.R` | Reporting-delay curve; onset-date and report-date datasets |
| `R/02_fit.R` | Maximum-likelihood fits, change-point profile, parameter draws, adequacy checks |
| `R/03_scenarios.R` | 9 scenarios x 1000 paired draws, policy surface |
| `R/04_stochastic.R` | Stochastic replicates |
| `R/05_sensitivity.R` | PRCC and 17 structural/assumption variants |
| `R/06_validation.R` | Out-of-sample forecast vs later official counts |
| `R/07_figures_tables.R` | Figures, LaTeX tables, `manuscript/numbers.tex` (all in-text numbers) |
| `taus_all_in_one.R` | The whole analysis + PDF build in a single script (generated) |
| `R/make_single_script.R` | Regenerates `taus_all_in_one.R` from the modular scripts |
| `quarto/` | `short_report.qmd`, `fit_report.qmd`, `manuscript.qmd` (+ rendered PDFs) |
| `R/08_build_reports.R` | Builds the three PDFs and checks the 3-page limit |
| `reports/` | `short_report.tex`, `fit_report.tex` (+ `out/` PDFs) |
| `tests/test_model.R` | Unit tests against analytic results |
| `manuscript/` | `main.tex`, `references.bib`, generated `numbers.tex`, `main.pdf` |
| `results/`, `figures/` | Generated outputs |
| `archive/` | Earlier 4-page Python version (superseded) |

## Caveats
* The baseline delay of 7 days comes from the study brief; the primary source could not be located. 4.6 and 8.6 days are run as sensitivity cases.
* Case counts do not identify isolation effectiveness; it is a scenario assumption.
* The `data/bvd_2026/README.md` asks that the files not be pasted into public AI tools. They are public national aggregates, but check that guidance before sharing the data further.
* Reference entries not marked as retrieved in `references.bib` should be checked against the publisher record.
